features.name: Scenario list navigation
features.notes: All 5 scenarios are listed in a sidebar list on the left (confirmed via UIA: '1) Input Events', '2) PointerPoint Properties', '3) Device Capabilities', '4) XAML Manipulations', '5) Gesture Recognizer'). Clicking each scenario loads the corresponding page. The selected scenario is visually highlighted with a blue background. The scenario names differ slightly from the rubric ('Input Events' vs full names) but all 5 are present and functional.

expected_behaviour_results.bullet: A list with 5 items is visible: 'Input Events', 'PointerPoint Properties', 'Device Capabilities', 'XAML Manipulations', 'Gesture Recognizer'
Clicking a scenario name loads the corresponding page content in the main area
The selected scenario is visually highlighted in the list

features.name: Pointer Pressed / Released interaction
features.notes: A 150x100 bordered rectangle labeled 'Pointer Pressed / Released' is displayed with LightGray background and black border. XAML source confirms PointerPressed/PointerReleased event handlers with RoyalBlue/LightGray color changes. The rectangle is present in UIA tree and visible in screenshot.

expected_behaviour_results.bullet: A 150×100 bordered rectangle labeled 'Pointer Pressed / Released' is displayed
Clicking/pressing the rectangle changes its background to blue and displays 'Pointer Pressed'
Releasing the pointer reverts the background to light grey and displays 'Pointer Released'

features.name: Pointer Enter / Exit interaction
features.notes: A 150x100 bordered rectangle labeled 'Pointer Enter / Exit' is displayed with LightGray background. XAML source confirms PointerEntered/PointerExited event handlers. The rectangle appears identically to the UWP source XAML. Visible in screenshot.

expected_behaviour_results.bullet: A 150×100 bordered rectangle labeled 'Pointer Enter / Exit' is displayed
Moving the pointer into the rectangle changes its background to blue and displays 'Pointer Entered'
Moving the pointer out of the rectangle reverts the background to light grey and displays 'Pointer Exited'

features.name: Tap / Double-Tap interaction
features.notes: A 150x100 bordered rectangle labeled 'Tap / Double-Tap' is present (confirmed via UIA text elements). XAML source defines Tapped/DoubleTapped event handlers with DeepSkyBlue/RoyalBlue color changes matching UWP behavior.

expected_behaviour_results.bullet: A 150×100 bordered rectangle labeled 'Tap / Double-Tap' is displayed
Single-clicking the rectangle changes its background to sky blue and displays 'Tapped'
Double-clicking the rectangle changes its background to royal blue and displays 'Double-Tapped'

features.name: Right-Tap / Press-and-Hold interaction
features.notes: A 150x100 bordered rectangle labeled 'Right-Tap / Press-and-Hold' is present (confirmed via UIA). XAML source defines RightTapped and Holding event handlers with proper color changes matching UWP behavior.

expected_behaviour_results.bullet: A 150×100 bordered rectangle labeled 'Right-Tap / Press-and-Hold' is displayed
Right-clicking the rectangle changes its background to blue and displays 'Right Tapped'
Press-and-hold changes background to sky blue and displays 'Holding', then reverts on release with 'Held'

features.name: Pointer properties display canvas
features.notes: Scenario 2 displays correctly with the instruction text 'Touch or click the screen to see information about the current pointer(s)' and a canvas area. The XAML defines a Canvas for displaying pointer popups. However, the canvas area appears mostly empty in the static screenshot — the popup only appears during active pointer interaction, which cannot be fully verified statically. The code and XAML structure are correct, matching UWP source.

expected_behaviour_results.bullet: A canvas area is displayed with instruction text 'Touch or click the screen to see information about the current pointer(s)'
Clicking on the canvas displays a popup near the click position showing pointer ID, X, Y coordinates, and contact state
The popup follows the pointer while the button/finger is held down
The popup disappears when the pointer is released

features.name: Mouse-specific pointer properties
features.notes: The code-behind (2-PointerPointProperties.xaml.cs) handles mouse-specific properties and displays them in red text when a mouse pointer is detected. This matches the UWP behavior. Cannot verify the red text color or specific property values in a static screenshot since the popup only appears during active interaction, but the code structure is faithful to the UWP original.

expected_behaviour_results.bullet: Mouse click on the canvas shows additional mouse-specific properties in red text
Properties include left button, right button, middle button, X1 button, X2 button states, and mouse wheel delta

features.name: Rectangle drag and rotate via XAML manipulation events
features.notes: Screenshot shows a light grey rectangle inside a canvas area. The XAML defines ManipulationMode with TranslateX, TranslateY, TranslateInertia, Rotate, RotateInertia. Code-behind handles ManipulationStarted (DeepSkyBlue), ManipulationInertiaStarting (RoyalBlue), and ManipulationCompleted (LightGray) events, matching UWP behavior.

expected_behaviour_results.bullet: A 200×200 light grey bordered rectangle is displayed inside a canvas area
Dragging the rectangle moves it across the canvas
The rectangle changes to blue during active manipulation
The rectangle reverts to light grey when manipulation completes

features.name: Movement axis ComboBox control
features.notes: UIA confirms a ComboBox named 'Movement Axis' is present. Screenshot shows 'X and Y' selected as default. XAML source defines three ComboBoxItem options: 'X and Y', 'X only', 'Y only' with SelectionChanged handler that modifies ManipulationMode.

expected_behaviour_results.bullet: A ComboBox labeled 'Movement Axis' is visible with 'X and Y' selected by default
Dropdown contains three options: 'X and Y', 'X only', 'Y only'
Selecting 'X only' restricts rectangle dragging to horizontal movement only
Selecting 'Y only' restricts rectangle dragging to vertical movement only

features.name: Inertia ToggleSwitch
features.notes: UIA shows a Button named 'Inertia' (which is the ToggleSwitch). Screenshot shows 'Inertia' label with a toggle switch set to 'On'. The toggle is functional. Marked partial because UIA exposes it as a Button rather than a proper ToggleSwitch automation pattern, though visually it appears correct with the blue 'On' state.

expected_behaviour_results.bullet: A ToggleSwitch labeled 'Inertia' is displayed and is on by default
Toggling it off disables inertia — the rectangle stops immediately when released
Toggling it on re-enables inertia — the rectangle glides after release

features.name: Reset button
features.notes: UIA confirms a Button named 'Reset' is present. The code-behind resets the rectangle position, ComboBox to 'X and Y', and Inertia toggle to on, matching UWP behavior.

expected_behaviour_results.bullet: A button labeled 'Reset' is visible
Clicking Reset moves the rectangle back to its original position
The Movement Axis ComboBox resets to 'X and Y'
The Inertia toggle resets to on
